description: A litigation director must approve an emergency preliminary-injunction filing against a former employee accused of taking confidential business information and must set the filing forum, injunction scope, evidence-preservation steps, and insurance conditions.

shared_context.S1: A former sales executive left the company last week and joined a direct competitor.
shared_context.S2: The company believes confidential customer information may have been used after the departure, and a preliminary-injunction hearing could be requested within three weeks.
shared_context.S3: The draft filing currently seeks broad relief concerning customer information, pricing materials, and source-code documentation.
shared_context.S4: Under the litigation team's pre-filing practice, the director conducts a case conference in which employment, forensics, and insurance counsel each report any material issue before the filing decision is signed; the director records authorization subject to stated prerequisites when a prerequisite must be completed before filing.

PF1.text: While checking the former executive's archived personnel file, Thomas found a signed separation agreement containing an exclusive forum clause requiring disputes about confidential information to be filed in the state court of the county where the executive worked; he has not yet added the clause to the draft strategy memorandum.

PF2.text: Nadia reviewed the access logs and forensic image this week and confirmed that the only company data copied to the executive's device was the customer-list database; the review did not show any copying of pricing materials or source-code documentation, and she has not updated the evidence chart yet.

PF3.text: Owen confirmed with the company's broker this week that the applicable cyber-and-crime endorsement requires the carrier's written consent before the company seeks injunctive relief against an employee; the confirmation is still outside the litigation file.

acceptance_conditions: The preliminary-injunction filing must be authorized.
The filing must be made in the state court of the county where the former executive worked.
The requested injunction must be limited to the customer-list database.
The carrier's written consent must be obtained before filing.
The original customer-list access logs and forensic image must be preserved under a documented hold.
The carrier-consent confirmation must be documented in the litigation file.

content_checks.C2: decisions['filing_forum'] in ['state court of the county where the executive worked', 'State court of the county where the executive worked', 'state_court_county_of_employment']
content_checks.C3: decisions['injunction_scope'] in ['customer-list database only', 'Customer-list database only', 'customer-list information only', 'Customer-list information only', 'customer-list only']
content_checks.C5: any(c['target'] == 'Nadia Chen' and c['type'] in ['evidence_update', 'directive', 'update evidence chart'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The signed separation agreement changes the filing forum from the draft's unspecified forum to the state court of the county where the former executive worked.

The forensic result changes the requested relief from broad protection for three information categories to customer-list-only relief and prompts Nadia's evidence-update commitment for the copied-data record.
The insurance endorsement changes the filing condition to obtaining written carrier consent beforehand and documenting that consent in the litigation file.
